messages:
Priya (CS): Hey team — NovaHealth hitting intermittent 429s during onboarding. They say it started after enabling our telemetry/diagnostics flag and doing concurrent SDK inits from mobile + web. Can we triage?
Sam (DevEx): Thanks — can you paste the most recent logs and the SDK version they use? Mobile is RN v3.2.1 and web is browser-sdk v1.8.0?
Priya (CS): Yep those are the versions. Log snippet from their staging run: 
```
2026-03-20T14:12:03Z INFO client-init tenant=novah client_id=nh-frontend conn=12
2026-03-20T14:12:03Z WARN rate-limiter code=429 msg=quota_exceeded window=60s client_id=nh-frontend
2026-03-20T14:12:03Z INFO telemetry upload start session=abc123
2026-03-20T14:12:04Z ERROR handshake failed status=429 attempt=1
```
Priya (CS): They run ~30 parallel inits per second in staging for stress tests.
Jordan (Eng): 30/s preflight/init is aggressive for ephemeral tokens. Is their client doing preflight per-tab?
NovaHealth - Alex: We spawn a new client for each user session (we thought ephemeral token reuse would be fine). Telemetry upload does a warm prefetch too.
Marta (Onboard): Two quick questions: are they doing a preflight token exchange for each connection? And are they calling the SDK init and immediately making requests (no splay)?
Priya (CS): Alex says yes to both — we didn't enforce reusing token across tabs.
Sam (DevEx): Ok likely a classic preflight fanout + telemetry warmup causing short 429 window. Workarounds we recommend: 1) coalesce preflight on the client (single token per origin), 2) add randomized splay on init (50-500ms), 3) exponential backoff on 429s with jitter.
Jordan (Eng): Also check we return Retry-After from rate-limiter. If not, clients must apply a secondary backoff. I'm seeing this pattern in our rate logs: multiple clients hammer token endpoint causing short-lived windowing.
ratelimit-bot: rate-limiter alert: tenant=novah spikes=27/s 429s=84 last_minute
Sam (DevEx): Quick example snippet to add to client init (pseudocode): 
```
async function initClient() {
  await sleep(randomBetween(50, 450)); // splay
  try {
    await preflight();
  } catch (e) {
    if (e.status === 429) {
      await sleep(backoffWithJitter());
      return initClient();
    }
    throw e;
  }
}
```
Priya (CS): Alex, can you try coalescing preflight on your side and enable reuse for the ephemeral token across tabs for staging?
NovaHealth - Alex: Will try coalescing tokens and add splay. Any quick server-side mitigation we can do while they patch?
Jordan (Eng): We can temporarily increase their rate bucket for onboarding (low-risk, time-limited). I'll open a reserve for 10 minutes while they test.
Marta (Onboard): Assigning temporary rate bump to eng-oncall. Also logging an enablement note for future customers to avoid per-tab preflight.
Sam (DevEx): Also send them this doc link — https://redwood.ai/docs/sdk/init#preflight-coalescing — includes client patterns and recommended delays.
Priya (CS): Action items: Alex to add coalescing + splay and report back (eta: 30m), Jordan to provision temporary rate bump (10m window) and monitor, Sam to follow up with docs snippet.
NovaHealth - Alex: Patch deployed (coalescing + 200-600ms splay). Initial test looks much better — no 429s in the next 60s. Thank you!
Jordan (Eng): I see their spike smoothed out in our dashboard and 429s dropped to 0. Rolling their temporary bump down in 5m.
Priya (CS): Awesome — I'll update the onboarding checklist to recommend default splay + token reuse for multi-tab apps.
Sam (DevEx): Postmortem note: add a short example in the quickstart showing a shared token store and splay helper.
Marta (Onboard): Closing loop with NovaHealth and capturing feedback for docs. :white_check_mark:
Priya (CS): Closing thread — reopen if they see recurrence.
